doc.title: Jake Hanna interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 11, 1997

title: Playing with Basie and Teddy Wilson; Jo Jones
summary: Easy to accompany Basie and Wilson; Jo Jones excellent but took over and was let go.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Oh, yeah, yeah, follow them. Just join in, have a ball. It’s like playing with Count Basie. Just join in, nothing to it with him. He was the easiest guy— Teddy Wilson, another guy, very easy to play with, very easy to play with. Just tag along man, that’s all, have a ball, enjoy his music. I was a customer to him, you know, a paid customer. I’d sit there and I’d play the brushes, and no other idiot drummer could get up there and screw him up. I just played very simple behind him. But Dahlender was very good with him and Jo Jones of course was absolutely phenomenal with Teddy. But then again Jo tried to take over that one too you know. That’s why Basie got rid of him, and that’s why Teddy had to get rid of him. Too bad too. He was the best of them all I guess.
Oh, yeah, yeah. No he was not a shy guy. Not shy at all.
No, not shy. He was a very good pal of mine. Six days a week I’d hang with that guy.
